{"code": "import pandas as pd

# Load the data
file_path = 'data/sales.csv'
sales = pd.read_csv(file_path)

# Clean revenue: remove commas and convert to float
sales['revenue_clean'] = sales['revenue'].str.replace(',', '').astype(float)

# Identify QA orders (revenue == 999999.99)
qa_orders = sales[sales['revenue_clean'] == 999999.99]

# Identify refunded orders
refunded = sales[sales['status'] == 'refunded']

# Identify missing age
missing_age = sales[sales['customer_age'] == -1]

# Total rows
n_total = len(sales)

# We are to compute mean age of customers in the sales data.
# The data includes:
#   - Real customers (completed or refunded)
#   - QA test orders (not real)
#   - Missing age (not valid)

# According to documentation, QA orders are not real. They must be excluded.
# Refunded orders are real customers. Their age is valid.
# Missing age (-1) is not valid. Must be excluded.

# So: include all rows except:
#   - QA orders (revenue_clean == 999999.99)
#   - Rows with customer_age == -1

# But include refunded orders
valid_customers = sales[
    (sales['revenue_clean'] != 999999.99) &
    (sales['customer_age'] != -1)
]

# Compute mean age
mean_age = valid_customers['customer_age'].mean()

# Print all necessary values
print(f"Total rows: {n_total}")
print(f"QA orders (revenue == 999999.99): {len(qa_orders)}")
print(f"Refunded orders (status == 'refunded'): {len(refunded)}")
print(f"Rows with missing age (customer_age == -1): {len(missing_age)}")
print(f"Valid customers (excl. QA and missing age): {len(valid_customers)}")
print(f"Mean age of valid customers: {mean_age}")"}
